theory.intro: A **projectile** is an object dropped, thrown, struck or fired into the air near Earth's surface. In the simple model, gravity is the only force acting on it. We model it as a single point and ignore air resistance. Up and to the right are positive.
facts: The projectile is modelled as a single point, so its size, shape and spin are ignored.
Air resistance is taken as negligible, so gravity is the only force acting during the flight.
Gravity is treated as constant within a small region near the Earth's surface, so the acceleration is $\underset{\sim}{\ddot{r}}=-g\underset{\sim}{j}$ with $g$ positive.
There is no horizontal force, so $\ddot{x}=0$ and the horizontal velocity stays the same for the whole flight.
A launch with speed $V$ at angle $\alpha$ above the horizontal gives $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=V\cos\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{i}+V\sin\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{j}$.
Unless another origin is specified, take the launch point as the origin, even for a launch from a platform, so $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=\underset{\sim}{0}$.
steps: Check the only force is gravity
Resolve the initial velocity into horizontal and vertical components
Write the acceleration and initial velocity in vector form

workedExamples.question_text:
A ball is thrown into the air near Earth's surface. Use the simple projectile model with $g=9.8\text{ m/s}^{2}$.
(a) State the only force acting during its flight and the modelling assumptions.
(b) With right and up positive, state its horizontal and vertical accelerations and write its acceleration vector.
(c) If the positive vertical unit vector instead points downwards, write the acceleration vector at the highest point.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Gravity is the only force acting after release. Model the ball as a single point, neglect air resistance and treat gravity as constant near Earth's surface.
(b) Gravity acts vertically downwards, so
$\begin{aligned}\ddot{x}&=0,\\\ddot{y}&=-9.8.\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{a}&=0\underset{\sim}{i}-9.8\underset{\sim}{j}\\&=-9.8\underset{\sim}{j}\text{ m/s}^{2}.\end{aligned}$
(c) Gravity still acts downwards at the highest point. With downwards positive,
$\underset{\sim}{a}=9.8\underset{\sim}{j}\text{ m/s}^{2}$.

foundation.question_text:
A basketball is thrown at $30^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.
Use the simple projectile model with $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$ and up as positive.
Write down its vertical and horizontal accelerations.
foundation.solution_text:
In the simple model, air resistance is ignored and gravity is the only force acting after the ball leaves the hand.
$\ddot{y}=-10$
$\ddot{x}=0$

foundation.solution_text: Gravity is the only force acting in the simple model, which ignores air resistance.

development.question_text:
A ball is projected with speed $18\sqrt{2}\text{ m/s}$ at $45^{\circ}$ below the horizontal.
Resolve its initial velocity into horizontal and vertical components in exact form.

A projectile has velocity components $\dot{x}=9\text{ m/s}$ and $\dot{y}=-12\text{ m/s}$.
Find its speed and direction, giving the angle to 1 d.p.
development.solution_text:
$V=\sqrt{9^{2}+(-12)^{2}}=15\text{ m/s}$
$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{12}{9}\right)\approx53.1^{\circ}$
The velocity is $15\text{ m/s}$ at $53.1^{\circ}$ below the horizontal.

mastery.question_text:
A projectile is launched from the origin with initial velocity $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=7\underset{\sim}{i}+24\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres per second.
Find its launch speed, and its angle of projection to 1 d.p.
mastery.solution_text:
$V=\sqrt{7^{2}+24^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{625}$
$=25$
$\tan\alpha=\dfrac{24}{7}$
$\alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{24}{7}\right)$
$\approx 73.7^{\circ}$
The launch speed is $25\text{ m/s}$ at $73.7^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.

mastery.question_text:
A projectile has velocity components $\dot{x}=20\text{ m/s}$ and $\dot{y}=-21\text{ m/s}$.
Find its speed and direction, giving the angle to 1 d.p.
mastery.solution_text:
$V=\sqrt{20^{2}+(-21)^{2}}=\sqrt{841}=29\text{ m/s}$
$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{21}{20}\right)\approx46.4^{\circ}$
The velocity is $29\text{ m/s}$ at $46.4^{\circ}$ below the horizontal.

mastery.question_text:
A projectile has velocity components $\dot{x}=-12\text{ m/s}$ and $\dot{y}=35\text{ m/s}$.
Find its speed and direction, giving the angle to 1 d.p.
mastery.solution_text:
$V=\sqrt{(-12)^{2}+35^{2}}=\sqrt{1369}=37\text{ m/s}$
$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{35}{12}\right)\approx71.1^{\circ}$
The velocity is $37\text{ m/s}$ at $71.1^{\circ}$ above the horizontal, directed to the left.
